name: Ecosystem and Relict Cultural Landscape of Lopé-Okanda
description: In central Gabon, where the Ogooué River cuts through the country, Lopé-Okanda is a patchwork of dense rainforest and open savannah left over from a cooler, drier past. Elephants and other endangered large mammals roam this mosaic. Hilltop settlements, caves and iron-working remains lie scattered across it, along with some 1,800 rock carvings that mark a route Bantu-speaking peoples once followed.
